about: What real players were measured doing with each instrument, baked from native/live/players-ranges.mjs by scripts/bake-players-ranges.mjs: never edited by hand.

pitch.what: The range of notes its players play (Clarinet in B-flat, written low E).

breath.what: The pressure in the mouths of two professional players, from their softest (pp) to their loudest (ff) at this note.

pulsation.what: The reed's resonance while a player plays it, the lip on it: 1825-2775 Hz. The reed alone, with no lip on it: 1530-2440 Hz.
pulsation.source: Chatziioannou & van Walstijn 2012; Chatziioannou 2010; Gaillard, Koehl & Gazengel 2024

qfactor.what: How lightly the reed is damped (its Q, no unit) while a player plays it: 1.6-32.8. The reed alone, with no lip on it: 30.0-50.0.
qfactor.source: Chatziioannou & van Walstijn 2012; Chatziioannou 2010; Gaillard, Koehl & Gazengel 2024

closing_pressure.what: The pressure that pushes the reed shut while a player plays it (its stiffness times its opening): 2247-3495 Pa. The reed's stiffness alone: 10.0, 25.0, 67.0 MPa per metre.
closing_pressure.source: Muñoz Arancón et al. 2016; Chatziioannou 2010; Gaillard, Koehl & Gazengel 2024 (Nederveen 1969)

contact_stifness.what: How much stiffer the reed grows as it bends towards the mouthpiece, measured while played: 3.7e+11 N/m⁴. This slider is something else: the model's stiffness once the reed is fully shut, which nobody has measured.

opening.what: How far the reed stood open at the mouthpiece's tip, at rest, under a player's lip: 0.26, 0.32, 0.34 mm.
opening.source: Chatziioannou & van Walstijn 2012; Chatziioannou 2010; Muñoz Arancón et al. 2016

lipForce.what: The lip's force on the reed while the note still plays, on a clarinet blown by an artificial mouth: from about 2 N, where it is usually played, eased to 0.3 N and pressed to 2.8 N, on written G4.

stroke.what: How long the tongue touches the reed, from portato to staccato, at two notes a second.

repeatRate.what: The fastest repeated notes with single tonguing: about 8 a second (about 11.5 with double tonguing).

litres.what: The air in one breath: 77 % of what wind players' lungs hold, from two standard deviations below the average to two above.
litres.source: Bouros et al. 2018; Cossette, Sliwinski & Macklem 2000

inhale.what: How long a breath takes to draw in: from reed players' quickest to a singer's full breath.
inhale.source: Fuks & Sundberg 1998; Salomoni, van den Hoorn & Hodges 2016
